Cochiti Pueblo

Cochiti’s own education and landscape accounts connect present-day Keres learning with responsibilities to future generations and to Kasha-Katuwe. An agency history supplies a separate, limited route into ancestral-pueblo and colonial-period context.

01

Identity and context

Cochiti Pueblo is a living Pueblo nation in New Mexico.

Read the sources [1] cochiti.org

02

A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Pueblo-published accounts, Keres language context, land and contemporary government. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] cochiti.org [2] New Mexico Legislature (host; document authorship not verified) [3] public-inspection.federalregister.gov

03

Education across generations

Cochiti’s Education Department presents language and culture alongside formal education. Its Language Nest supports family teaching, while the summer youth programme brings fluent Keres teachers and developing teacher assistants together. The page also describes adult learning, higher education assistance and community library services; these descriptions are programme aims rather than measured outcomes.

Read the sources [4] Pueblo de Cochiti

04

Kasha-Katuwe as a living landscape

The Pueblo’s account explains Kasha-Katuwe as a place of continuing community relationships and stewardship. BLM’s separate outline places ancestral pueblos, Spanish arrival and the Pueblo Revolt within a broader historical sequence. The dated landscape photograph introduces this specifically identified place; it does not establish a boundary or permission to enter.

Read the sources [5] Pueblo de Cochiti [6] Bureau of Land Management

Tent Rocks — selected Pueblo account of cultural landscape and stewardship ↗

Cochiti explains Kasha-Katuwe as a continuing cultural landscape and describes stewardship as a responsibility carried across generations.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual About the Monument opening two paragraphs and concluding stewardship paragraphs: reader lines 2–3 and 46–47. Visitor rules were encountered but are not reproduced as access advice.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal community-page body read. Oral histories and traditional teachings are mentioned in general; no underlying narrative, ceremonial practice, restricted place or present boundary is documented here.

Kasha-Katuwe history and nature — selected agency historical context ↗

The agency relates ancestral pueblos and Cochiti continuity to the monument landscape, placing Spanish arrival and the Pueblo Revolt in a short historical outline.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual History and Cultural Significance two-paragraph body, with adjoining public landscape context. Underlying archaeological surveys and colonial records were not read.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal HTTP 200 HTML/text read; the search reader also exposed a www-26 mirror, but this canonical URL was separately obtained successfully. This agency interpretation does not establish precise territorial boundaries.
